common_name: Spring Gold Beautyberry (Golden New-Leaf Purple Beautyberry)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial shade; Spring Gold is a foliage-focused selection of purple beautyberry whose new leaves emerge a bright golden-yellow before settling to green as the season progresses.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to partial afternoon shade, siting the shrub where its color-changing spring foliage will be visible up close. Spring Gold opens each season with a flush of vividly golden-yellow new leaves that gradually mature to a more typical green, giving this cultivar two distinct seasons of interest — a spring foliage show followed by the usual fall display of violet-purple berries along arching branches. Because color intensity is strongest on fresh growth, a hard late-winter pruning back to a framework of low buds encourages a fuller flush of golden new leaves the following spring in addition to heavier fruit set. Give it consistent moisture during the spring growth flush to keep the gold coloration from fading prematurely in heat.

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in partial shade to full sun; Splashy is a compact, foliage-driven beautyberry selected in Japan for leaves that are more than half overlaid in stable white variegation.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in partial shade, which helps prevent scorch on the heavily white-splashed leaf surface while still allowing the variegation to read clearly against the darker green leaf base. Splashy grows lower and more compact than typical purple beautyberry, valued primarily for its dramatically patterned foliage that carries the display from spring through fall rather than for fruit, since berry set is noticeably sparser than on green-leaved selections. Remove any shoots that revert to solid green promptly, cutting them back to the variegated wood, so the plant does not gradually lose its patterned character. Light, shaping pruning in late winter is usually sufficient, since this cultivar is grown chiefly as a season-long foliage accent rather than for heavy berry production.

common_name: Wine Spritzer Beautyberry (Cream, Green and Pink Variegated Beautyberry)

planting.note: Plant container shrubs in spring in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to light shade; Wine Spritzer (sold under the cultivar name 'Shiji Murasaki') is a Japanese-origin beautyberry grown for reticulated cream, green, and pink new-growth foliage rather than heavy fruiting.

directions: Plant in well-drained, moderately fertile soil, giving it full sun for the most saturated foliage color or light afternoon shade in hot climates to conserve moisture and reduce leaf stress. Wine Spritzer opens with cream-yellow leaves on reddish new stems in spring, and the foliage develops an unusual mottled, reticulated pattern of white, green, and pink as it ages, making this cultivar a season-long foliage specimen more than a fruiting shrub, since its clusters of pale lavender summer flowers give way to only a sparse showing of violet berries. Because flowers and berries form on new wood, cutting the arching stems back hard in late winter renews vigorous colorful growth and keeps the shrub from becoming leggy. Site it as a specimen or accent where its unusual variegated foliage can be appreciated up close rather than relying on it for a heavy fall berry display.
